label: nyiso 25 rcpf-steep (PROBE)
definition: PROBE (rejected, not a keeper). Tests the bucket-A #1 scarcity hypothesis: steepen the NYISO locational RCPF reserve demand curves from the linear-ramp-to-zero stand-in to the published top-25%-span shape (critical_mw = 0.75 x requirement; FERC ER21-502 sets the NYCA 30-min $750 max at 1,965 = 0.75 x 2,620), plus the Ravenswood steam-HR correction. Finding: the steeper published curve DEEPENS the downstate tail faithfully (NYC max $138->$890, 2023 14h >$300) but does NOT add C3c tail HOURS (2024 0h, 2025 12h, unchanged) because the tail COUNT is incidence-gated by the model’s too-loose downstate reserve headroom (idle NYC peakers provide ample reserve; perfect-foresight import over-service backs down downstate gas), not by the demand-curve slope. The deeper few-hour spikes push C3a mean LMP to +12% (over the +-8% band) for no C3c gain. CONCLUSION: the RCPF demand-curve SHAPE is not the C3c lever; the lever is downstate reserve INCIDENCE (locational headroom / import discipline) — the documented next structural step, out of scope as it would touch the nyiso-24 import reconciliation. The curve steepening is therefore NOT carried into the keeper (nyiso 25 steam-merit), which retains only the Ravenswood merit-order fix.
